page: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage, relying instead on remote Premium Storage, and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this server mostly in the average tier, with some notable exceptions. The Neoverse-N2 processor delivers average single-core and multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, but shows weakness in ray tracing and extended instruction sets. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10%, despite AES hardware flag support. However, memory subsystem performance is strong, as evidenced by a top 25% PassMark memory score and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.04 GB/sec.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the E4ps_v6 offers a memory-optimized profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory capacity without the expense of high core counts. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis (achieving 8.3 million operations per second in benchmarks), static web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. It is less suitable for heavy cryptographic tasks, complex vector math, or GPU-accelerated workloads.
